messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test `testLargeSample` exercises the PolynomialFitter with large sample sizes (40,000 points) and polynomial degrees up to 9. The test adds observed points and fits a polynomial function using the LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer. According to the current bug report, a serious issue arises when large numbers of weights are used with multivariate vector optimizers: internally, a full nxn matrix is created and copied where n is the number of weights. This leads to memory exhaustion for large n (e.g., 4120 points).

In the test, the large number of data points (40000) leads to a large number of weights internally when fitting, triggering this problem.

The `PolynomialFitter.fit(double[] guess)` method delegates to `fit(ParametricUnivariateFunction, double[])`, which presumably calls the underlying optimizer methods. The problem lies in that the weight representation to the optimizer of the curve fitting process uses an inefficient full matrix for what should be sparse diagonal weights, thus consuming excessive memory.

Since the `PolynomialFitter` is designed to work with a curve fitter that uses weights corresponding to observations, the internal representation of weights in the multivariate vector optimizers, as highlighted in the bug report, causes infeasible memory usage and failures with large sample sizes.

This aligns with the test failure and the bug report describing memory exhaustion. The large matrix copying is triggered by the large number of weights when fitting large samples with the current implementation of multivariate vector optimizers that expect a weight matrix instead of a simple weight vector representation.

Recent bug reports do not provide further relevant details, so the diagnosis based on the current report and test is that the PolynomialFitter's usage of weights and its interaction with the LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer results in an internal full nxn weight matrix creation that is memory-prohibitive for large datasets.

Hence, the root cause is the use or conversion of weight vectors into full nxn weight matrices in multivariate vector optimizers when fitting large datasets, which causes memory exhaustion, leading to the failing test case.

The fix should involve optimizing or changing the internal weight handling in the fitting or optimizer classes to avoid full matrix creation and switching to sparse or diagonal representations where appropriate.

This is why the `testLargeSample` fails with large datasets and why the summary mentions not being able to use new multivariate vector optimizers with large number of weights.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
